task_name: Land Mutation (Dakhil Kharij / Namantaran) — recording change of ownership in the land record
citizen_input: Application to record a transfer (sale/gift/inheritance) with registered sale-deed / succession documents, filed at the Tehsil
outcome: Khatauni (record of rights) amended to reflect the new owner; certified copy of updated khatauni issued
legal_basis: UP Revenue Code 2006 (ss. 33, 34, 35) / UP Land Records Manual
total_days: ~35-45 days (45-day disposal deadline enforced by state directive; longer if contested)
source: UP Revenue Code 2006, s.35 (mutation; proclamation; uncontested/contested; appeal to SDO within 30 days); UP Revenue Code 2006 ss.33-35 bare act; 45-day dakhil kharij disposal deadline (state directive)

task_name: Ration Card (New / Member Addition) under NFSA
citizen_input: Application form + Aadhaar, residence/income proof, family details via e-district/CSC/Supply Office
outcome: Ration card issued (priority/AAY category) with a Fair Price Shop assigned
legal_basis: National Food Security Act 2013 (ss. 10, 12, 14, 16); state TPDS Control Order; e-district
total_days: 30 days statutory (NFSA inspection/verification norm); card collectable up to ~45 days in practice
source: National Food Security Act 2013 (ss.10,12,14,16); Uttarakhand FCS Dept URCMS / e-PDS ration-card process; NFSA 30-day inspection/verification norm; DGRO -> State Food Commission appeal

task_name: Register a birth and obtain a birth certificate for a newborn
citizen_input: How do I register a birth and get a birth certificate for my newborn?
outcome: A registered birth event and a QR-verified digital birth certificate issued by the Municipal Corporation's Registrar of Births and Deaths via the CRS portal (dc.crsorgi.gov.in), usable as single proof of date of birth.
legal_basis: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (Act 18 of 1969), esp. ss. 8, 10, 12, 13, 17, 23-25, as amended by the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (Act 20 of 2023, in force 01-Oct-2023, mandating digital registration via the Civil Registration System); delivery timeline and appeals under the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (U.P. Act 3 of 2011) / applicable State Right-to-Public-Services scheme.
total_days: 7 days (statutory registration window: 21 days from birth to report free of charge; certificate delivery within the State Right-to-Service window, commonly 7 working days)

task_name: Caste / Income / Domicile Certificate issuance
citizen_input: Online application via e-District/CSC (or at Tehsil) with self-declaration, ID, address and supporting proofs
outcome: Digitally-signed caste / income / domicile certificate delivered to the applicant
legal_basis: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (Right to Public Services) / e-District UP
total_days: ~7-15 working days (statutory limit under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam schedule)
source: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (Right to Public Services; first appeal 30 days, second appeal 60 days); e-District UP income/caste/domicile process & Lekhpal verification timelines

task_name: RTE 25% EWS/DG Free-Seat Admission in a Private Unaided School
citizen_input: Parent's online application for an EWS/DG free seat (child's birth proof, income/caste certificate, residence proof, distance declaration)
outcome: Child admitted free of cost to a private unaided school against a reserved 25% seat, reimbursed by the state
legal_basis: RTE Act 2009 s.12(1)(c)
total_days: ~45-60 days (registration window to reporting/admission)
source: RTE Act 2009 s.12(1)(c) and s.12(2); Uttarakhand RTE online admission portal (registration, BEO verification, lottery, allotment)

task_name: MGNREGA Job Card Issue and Guaranteed Work Demand
citizen_input: Household application for a job card at the Gram Panchayat, then a dated written application demanding work
outcome: Job card issued and wage employment provided within 15 days (else unemployment allowance), with wages paid within 15 days of work
legal_basis: MGNREGA 2005 s.3
total_days: ~30 days job-card issue to first wage payment (15 to allot work + 15 to pay wages)
source: MGNREGA 2005 s.3 (15-day work guarantee), s.3(1) unemployment allowance, s.3(3) delayed-wage compensation 0.05%/day; MGNREGA Operational Guidelines 2013 (muster roll, measurement book, GRS/JE roles, wage FTO, social audit)

task_name: Register a Death and Obtain a Death Certificate
citizen_input: A family member has died and I need to register the death and get the official death certificate.
outcome: Death registered in the Civil Registration System and an official death certificate issued to the informant/next of kin.
legal_basis: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (ss. 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 17) as amended by the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (No. 20 of 2023, in force 1 Oct 2023, mandating CRS-portal registration and digital certificates); state RBD Rules; UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act (time-bound delivery + appeal ladder).
total_days: Certificate issued free within 7 days of registration completion (RBD Act s.17); registration itself normally same-day when reported within 21 days. Delayed cases add the s.13 permission/order timeline.

task_name: Building Plan / Housing Construction Permit (Naksha Sanction) in a Nagar Nigam
citizen_input: Building plan drawings (CAD/AutoDCR), site/ownership documents, application fee via the OBPAS single-window portal
outcome: Sanctioned building plan + permit/sanction letter authorizing construction
legal_basis: UP Building Construction & Development Bye-Laws 2008; UP Urban Planning & Development Act 1973; Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011; OBPAS/AutoDCR
total_days: 15-30 days statutory (15 via OBPAS auto-scrutiny; 30 under Building Bye-Laws)
source: UP Building Construction & Development Bye-Laws 2008 (amended 2016); UP OBPAS/AutoDCR single-window portal; Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (Right to Public Services)

task_name: Disability (Divyang) Certificate and UDID Card
citizen_input: How do I get a disability (divyang) certificate and UDID card to access benefits?
outcome: A digitally-signed disability certificate (Form V/VI/VII) stating the assessed percentage, and a nationally-valid UDID card downloadable from the portal with a physical PVC card by post; usable to claim RPwD reservations, pension, scholarships, and concessions.
legal_basis: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, Sections 56-59 (certifying authority, certificate valid across country, appeal); RPwD Rules, 2017, Rule 18 (Forms V/VI/VII/VIII, one-month issuance, ninety-day appeal); Gazette Notification S.O. 76(E) dated 04.01.2018 (assessment guidelines for 21 disabilities); UDID scheme of DEPwD (swavlambancard.gov.in). In UP, delivery is assisted via e-District / Jan Seva Kendra (CSC).
total_days: Approx. 30 days statutory for certificate issuance from receipt (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3)); physical UDID PVC card typically an additional 30-60 days.

task_name: New domestic electricity connection for a house
citizen_input: Applicant's address and sanctioned load required (kW); ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID/Passport/PAN); proof of ownership/occupancy of premises (registered sale deed / partition / succession / heir certificate, or rent agreement + owner NOC); recent photograph; mobile number and email; APL/BPL category.
outcome: A metered, energized domestic electricity connection released by the area DISCOM (in UP: a UPPCL DISCOM such as PVVNL/MVVNL/PuVVNL/DVVNL; in Uttarakhand: UPCL) at the sanctioned load, after payment of the demand-note charges and security deposit.
legal_basis: Electricity Act, 2003 (s.43 universal duty to supply); Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020 (as amended); UP Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (UPERC) governing application, demand note and release timelines (cl. 4.15/4.16) — in Uttarakhand, UERC Electricity Supply Code; UPERC (Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum & Electricity Ombudsman) Regulations, 2022 for appeals. Delivered via the Jhatpat Connection Scheme portal (upenergy.in).
total_days: ~7 days (domestic, no line extension) to ~15-30 days; Jhatpat scheme targets ~10 days

task_name: Apply for the Old-Age (Vridha) Pension for a senior citizen with no regular income
citizen_input: How do I apply for the old-age (vridha) pension as a senior citizen with no regular income?
outcome: A monthly old-age pension (UP SSPY: currently ~Rs 1,000/month; Uttarakhand: Rs 1,500/month) is sanctioned by the District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer and credited quarterly to the applicant's Aadhaar-linked bank account by DBT/NEFT.
legal_basis: Delivered as the state Social Security / Vridhavastha Pension (Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana, SSPY, in UP) layered on the central Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP); time-bound-delivery and appeal backstopped by the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (UP Act 3 of 2011) / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act. Administered by the state Department of Social Welfare / Directorate of Social Welfare via the Integrated Pension Portal (sspy-up.gov.in / ssp.uk.gov.in).
total_days: Approx. 30-60 days from complete application to sanction; pension then paid quarterly via NEFT/DBT.

task_name: Widow / Destitute Woman (Nirashrit Mahila) Pension after husband's death
citizen_input: How do I get a widow (nirashrit mahila) pension after my husband's death?
outcome: Applicant's name is added to the widow-pension roll and ₹1,000/month (₹500 state + ₹500 central) is disbursed quarterly (₹3,000) by DBT into her Aadhaar-linked bank account.
legal_basis: UP Nirashrit Mahila (Widow) Pension Scheme administered by the Women Welfare Department (Mahila Kalyan Vibhag) via the Integrated Social Pension Portal (sspy-up.gov.in); registration of husband's death under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969; income/domicile certificates and service time-limits under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (Right to Public Services); disbursement via DBT/PFMS.
total_days: Approx. 90-120 days end-to-end once prerequisite certificates are in hand (verification 45 days + block review 15 days + district-committee sanction ~30 days + PFMS/DBT ~30 days); prerequisite certificates add 7-30 days.

task_name: Correct or change name and address on Aadhaar after marriage
citizen_input: Aadhaar number; registered mobile (for OTP); marriage certificate; proof of identity in new name (name change); proof of address in new name or HoF's proof + proof of relationship (address change).
outcome: Updated Aadhaar with corrected name and address; downloadable e-Aadhaar PDF; SRN/URN issued for tracking.
legal_basis: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016, s.54; Aadhaar (Enrolment and Update) Regulations, 2016 (No. 2 of 2016) — demographic-update provisions and Schedule of acceptable documents. Administered by UIDAI, a central statutory authority.
total_days: 30 days typical (90% within 30 days); up to 90 days outer bound

task_name: Convert agricultural farmland to residential use (Section 143 land-use change), Uttarakhand
citizen_input: I own agricultural farmland in Uttarakhand and want to build a house on it — how do I get the plot legally converted (bhu-upyog parivartan) from agricultural to residential use before I start construction?
outcome: A Section 143 declaration/conversion order from the SDM reclassifying the plot from agricultural (krishi) to non-agricultural/residential use, with the change entered in the revenue record (khatauni) — after which a separate building-map (naksha) sanction is still required before construction.
legal_basis: Section 143 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 (as adopted/applicable in Uttarakhand) — declaration of use of an agricultural holding for residential/industrial purposes; conversion administered by the Revenue Department (SDM/Assistant Collector, Tehsildar) via the landuse.uk.gov.in portal. Building sanction falls under the local body / development-authority building bye-laws (separate track).
total_days: Statutory SOP target ~15-40 working days including the mandatory 21-day public-objection window; realistic average 4-7 months when records are clean; contested/forest-adjacent plots longer.

task_name: Get your family's Ayushman Bharat (PMJAY) health card for free hospital treatment
citizen_input: Family details plus one member's Aadhaar and registered mobile; ration card / family ID; for Uttarakhand any proof of permanent residence.
outcome: Ayushman card issued for each eligible family member, enabling cashless secondary/tertiary treatment up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year (universal for all residents in Uttarakhand under AAUY; SECC/state-list-based in UP, plus universal 70+ cover) at empanelled hospitals.
legal_basis: Ayushman Bharat PMJAY — executive scheme of National Health Authority under MoHFW (Cabinet approval 2018), implemented in UP via SACHIS and in Uttarakhand as the state-universal Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana (AAUY) converged with PMJAY. Not a statute; no Right-to-Public-Services SLA attaches. Ayushman Vay Vandana vertical (Oct 2024 approval) adds universal cover for all citizens aged 70+.
total_days: Same-day to 15 days (self-eKYC often auto-approved instantly; State Health Agency manual review of mismatches can take days; no statutory SLA)

task_name: Register a newborn's birth and obtain an official birth certificate (UP / Uttarakhand, urban / Nagar Nigam area)
citizen_input: Reporting form / hospital birth-report (Form 1) with baby's name (if chosen), sex, date & place of birth, parents' names and address, parents' + informant's Aadhaar; for late cases: affidavit, supporting proof (hospital/immunization/school record), and prescribed late fee.
outcome: A registered birth entry in the Civil Registration System and an official digital birth certificate (Form 6) issued by the Nagar Nigam Registrar, downloadable from CRS / the state e-district portal.
legal_basis: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (Act 18 of 1969), ss. 8-13, 17, 23, 25, as amended by the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (Act 20 of 2023), in force 1 Oct 2023; respective UP and Uttarakhand Registration of Births and Deaths Rules; UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 / Uttarakhand right-to-services notification for time-bound issuance.
total_days: Same-day to 7 days if reported within 21 days; longer for delayed/late tiers (30-day, 1-year, and post-1-year magistrate-order routes).

task_name: Free routine immunization for a newborn and issuance of the immunization (MCP) card
citizen_input: "Where do I get my newborn's free routine vaccinations and an immunization card in my area?"
outcome: Child registered under UIP (paper MCP card + U-WIN digital record), birth doses and the primary series administered free at a government session site, with each dose and next due-date recorded.
legal_basis: Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), Government of India (National Health Mission), delivering free vaccines under the National Immunization Schedule against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases; Mother and Child Protection (MCP) Card as the statutory record; U-WIN — the national electronic immunization registry (MoHFW) — for digital registration, appointment booking and QR e-Vaccination Certificate. Delivered through the state NHM (UP / Uttarakhand) Routine Immunization division under the District Chief Medical Officer / District Immunization Officer. Not derived from a Right-to-Public-Services (Sewa Adhikar) time-bound schedule: routine immunization is a walk-in entitlement, not an application-driven certified service.
total_days: Ongoing per the National Immunization Schedule: birth doses at/near birth; primary series at 6, 10, 14 weeks; boosters at 9-12 months and 16-24 months. No statutory turnaround for a single visit; card issued same-day at first session.

task_name: Get a disability certificate and UDID card assessed at the district hospital
citizen_input: Applicant identity/Aadhaar, passport photo, address proof, and any existing medical/diagnostic records for the claimed disability; online UDID registration.
outcome: Disability Certificate (Form V) with assessed disability type and percentage, plus the Unique Disability ID (UDID) card (Form VI / colour-coded Form VII), issued through the UDID portal after Medical Board assessment.
legal_basis: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (ss. 56-59); RPwD Rules, 2017, Rule 18 (as amended by RPwD Amendment Rules, 2024) — Disability Certificate (Form V), UDID card (Form VI / colour-coded Form VII); UDID scheme, DEPwD. Uttar Pradesh delivery via e-District UP / divyangjanUP integrated with the national UDID portal.
total_days: Up to 90 days (3 months) statutory limit for certificate + UDID card issuance under Rule 18 (as amended 2024); physical card dispatch may lag.

task_name: Apply for the monthly disability pension (Divyang/Viklang pension) using a disability certificate
citizen_input: A person 18+ holding a 40%+ disability certificate, resident of the state, family income within the rural/urban ceiling, with Aadhaar-linked bank account, seeking the recurring monthly disability pension via Direct Benefit Transfer.
outcome: Beneficiary enrolled on the state social-security pension roll; monthly disability pension (UP Rs 1,000/month paid quarterly; Uttarakhand Rs 1,200-1,500/month) credited to the Aadhaar-linked bank account by DBT.
legal_basis: Administered by the state Department for Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (UP: Divyangjan Sashaktikaran Vibhag) / Social Welfare Department under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (40%+ benchmark disability); delivered as a notified state pension scheme via the integrated pension portal (UP: sspy-up.gov.in; Uttarakhand: ssp.uk.gov.in / eSPAN); UP service-delivery covered by the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.
total_days: 30-90 days typical (complete application to first credit); not a uniform statutory deadline for pension sanction

task_name: Get a Protection Order against Domestic Violence from the Court
citizen_input: Aggrieved woman's identity/address proof; details of the domestic relationship (shared household) with the respondent; a written account of the abuse (physical/sexual/verbal/emotional/economic) with dates; any evidence (medical records, photos, messages, witnesses); Domestic Incident Report if already recorded by a Protection Officer/service provider.
outcome: A Protection Order under Section 18 (and, as sought, residence/monetary/custody/compensation orders under ss.19-22) issued by the Magistrate restraining the respondent, enforceable by police; breach is a cognizable offence under Section 31.
legal_basis: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (Act 43 of 2005) - esp. ss. 4, 8-9, 12, 13, 18-23, 27, 28, 29, 31; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Rules, 2006 (Forms I-IV, Rules 5, 6, 12). National law in force in Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
total_days: First hearing within 3 days of filing; disposal endeavoured within 60 days (Section 12). Interim/ex parte relief possible same day under Section 23.
source: https://blog.ipleaders.in/domestic-violence-act/; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2021 (Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - full text); Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Rules, 2006 (Ministry of Women & Child Development); https://wcd.nic.in/act/protection-women-domestic-violence-act-2005

task_name: Apply for a Domicile / Residence Certificate (Nivas Praman Patra)
citizen_input: Applicant's identity (Aadhaar), address and residence proofs (ration card / electricity or water bill / rent-property record), age/birth proof, passport photo, and a self-declaration affidavit of residence; a student/minor uses a parent's residence proof plus school records. Applying for state-quota college admission or state-domicile reservation in a government job.
outcome: A digitally signed Nivas Praman Patra (domicile/residence certificate) confirming ordinary/permanent residence in the state, downloadable from the e-District portal, usable for state-quota education seats and state-domicile job reservation. In UP it is lifetime-valid.
legal_basis: Revenue Department issuance under the district Collectorate; service delivery time-guaranteed under the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (UP Act No. 3 of 2011) and, in Uttarakhand, the Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar Adhiniyam, 2011. Residence-eligibility rules are set by state revenue-department rules.
total_days: 15 working days (statutory; commonly cited 15-30)

task_name: Obtain a trade licence from the Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam) to legally run a business
citizen_input: Applicant's identity & address proof, business premises proof (ownership deed or rent agreement + owner's NOC), property-tax/holding number of the premises, trade category details, and category-specific clearances (fire NOC, FSSAI food licence, UPPCB consent) where the trade requires them.
outcome: A trade licence issued by the Nagar Nigam authorising the applicant to legally run the specified trade at the declared premises (typically annual, renewable before expiry).
legal_basis: Uttar Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1959 (licensing of premises for trades / dangerous & offensive trades; Municipal Commissioner as licensing authority); service delivery via UP e-Nagar Sewa portal; timelines/appeals under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam (Right to Public Services), 2011. In UP the corporation trade licence is distinct from the "gumasta" (Shops & Establishments registration under the UP Dookan Aur Vanijya Adhishthan Adhiniyam, 1962, Labour Dept).
total_days: Typically ~7-30 days from a complete application where notified under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam / corporation citizen charter (indicative; exact SLA varies by corporation and trade).
source: https://e-nagarsewaup.gov.in/ (UP e-Nagar Sewa - Urban Local Body citizen services portal, Directorate of Local Bodies, Govt of UP); https://jansunwai.up.nic.in/ (UP Jansunwai-Samadhan grievance redressal portal - verified: municipal-service escalation with reminders on deadline lapse); https://niveshmitra.up.nic.in/ (UP Nivesh Mitra single-window - integrates trade/establishment clearances); Utta

task_name: Factory licence and registration for a manufacturing unit in Uttarakhand (Factories Act, 1948)
citizen_input: Constituted legal entity (proprietorship/partnership/LLP/company) with PAN, GST and bank account; site details, occupier and manager particulars, worker headcount, connected power load (HP/kW), approved building plan and layout, and manufacturing process description.
outcome: Registration of the factory and a licence to operate granted under the Factories Act, 1948 (with the ride-along pollution, labour and safety clearances needed to lawfully run the unit).
legal_basis: Factories Act, 1948 (Sec. 2(m) definition, Sec. 6 plan approval/licensing rules, Sec. 7 occupier notice) and the Uttarakhand Factories Rules made thereunder; Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 (Sec. 25) and Air (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 (Sec. 21) for UEPPCB consents; ESI Act 1948, EPF & MP Act 1952, Contract Labour (R&A) Act 1970 for labour registrations; Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (Sewa Ka Adhikar) for time-bound delivery and appeals.
total_days: Roughly 90-180 days end to end; pollution consent and Factories-Act plan approval are the long poles (exact per-service limits set by Uttarakhand's Right-to-Service notifications, not independently confirmed this session).
source: https://labour.uk.gov.in/ (Uttarakhand Labour Department / Directorate of Factories, Boilers, Labour & Employment); https://ueppcb.uk.gov.in/ (Uttarakhand Environment Protection & Pollution Control Board - Consent to Establish / Operate); https://investuttarakhand.uk.gov.in/ (Invest Uttarakhand single-window facilitation); https://edistrict.uk.gov.in/ (Uttarakhand e-District services); Factories A

task_name: File an FIR at a police station when police refuse to register your complaint
citizen_input: Written complaint describing a cognizable offence (what happened, when, where, who), complainant's name/address/contact, ID proof, and any evidence; postal receipt kept at each escalation.
outcome: FIR registered for the cognizable offence and a free copy handed to the complainant; if police still refuse, a Magistrate orders registration and investigation under BNSS S.175(3) or proceeds on the complaint.
legal_basis: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 (in force 01-07-2024): S.173 (information in cognizable cases; electronic/e-FIR, Zero FIR, free copy, 14-day preliminary enquiry for 3-7 yr offences), S.173(4) (escalation to Superintendent of Police on SHO refusal), S.175(3) (Magistrate power to order registration/investigation), S.223 (Magistrate taking cognizance of a complaint). Read with UP Police CCTNS e-FIR/citizen services and UPRTPS/Jansunwai grievance mechanisms.
total_days: FIR itself is immediate for cognizable offences; escalation remedies take days to a few weeks depending on the authority.

task_name: File an FIR / escalate when a police station refuses to register a cognizable-offence complaint (Uttar Pradesh)
citizen_input: Oral or written account of the offence; identity/contact details; for the electronic/e-FIR route a signature furnished within 3 days; for SP/magistrate escalation a copy of the earlier complaint and proof it was submitted (registered-post receipt); for the magistrate application an affidavit and copies of the SHO and SP complaints.
outcome: FIR registered against a free copy issued to the complainant, and investigation of the cognizable offence commenced — either at the station, or after SP direction, or on magistrate order.
legal_basis: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 — s.173(1) (mandatory FIR registration for cognizable offences, free copy, zero-FIR, electronic information), s.173(3) (14-day preliminary enquiry only for 3-7 year offences), s.174 (non-cognizable), s.173(4) (complaint to Superintendent of Police on refusal), s.175(3) (Magistrate's power to direct registration/investigation), s.223 (private complaint on oath); Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P. (2014) 2 SCC 1 (registration mandatory); U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (service-guarantee appeal clocks).
total_days: Registration at the station is same-day / immediate under s.173(1); the SP (s.173(4)) and Magistrate (s.175(3)) routes have no hard statutory day-count in BNSS. Where the grievance is routed as a service default, the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam gives a 30-day first-appeal and 60-day second-appeal window.

task_name: File a complaint about adulterated or unsafe food sold by a shop or restaurant
citizen_input: Complaint about adulterated / unsafe / substandard / misbranded food from a shop or restaurant, with details: FBO name and address, date/time of purchase, product, bill/receipt, wrapper, retained sample and photographs if available.
outcome: Complaint registered and tracked (unique concern number); sample lifted and lab-tested; on an adverse Food Analyst report, penalty via the Adjudicating Officer or prosecution of the food business operator in the Special Court, with refund of analysis fee to the complainant if non-compliant.
legal_basis: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSS Act) and Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011; consumer right to get food analysed under Section 40 FSS Act r/w Rule 2.4.4; sampling and Food Analyst report under Sections 38, 42, 46-47 and Rule 2.4 (analyst report within 14 days); adjudication under Section 68 (Adjudicating Officer, ADM rank) and prosecution in Special Court under Section 69/Section 51-59; administered in Uttar Pradesh by the Food Safety & Drug Administration (FSDA) under the Commissioner of Food Safety, with Designated Officer and Food Safety Officer at district level.
total_days: Registration immediate; Food Analyst report within 14 days of sample receipt; adjudication/prosecution timeline not statutorily fixed (varies).

task_name: Apply for a Learner's Licence and then a Permanent Driving Licence at the RTO
citizen_input: Aadhaar/proof of age, proof of address, passport photos, self-declaration of physical fitness (Form 1) or medical certificate (Form 1A where required); a vehicle of the applied class for the driving test.
outcome: A Learner's Licence (Form 3, valid 6 months), then after passing the driving test a smart-card Permanent Driving Licence for the vehicle class applied for.
legal_basis: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (ss. 7-9); Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (Rr. 10-11 learner licence/Form 2, R. 15 minimum 30-day interval, R. 14/Form 4 driving licence). Uttar Pradesh Motor Vehicles Rules, 1998 administer state procedure/fees; service timelines under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 where scheduled.
total_days: Stage 1: same day to a few days for the LL; then mandatory 30-day gap; Stage 2: driving-test slot plus 1-3 days for card dispatch.

task_name: Get a legal heir / varasat certificate to claim a deceased family member's property and dues
citizen_input: A family member has died; I need to establish myself as legal heir (varasat) to claim the deceased's property (land/house) and dues (pension, bank, gratuity, insurance).
outcome: Varasat recorded in revenue records (khatauni) naming legal heirs — enabling property transfer; plus a Surviving Member / legal-heir certificate to claim dues, pension and benefits.
legal_basis: UP Revenue Code 2006 §§33-35 (varasat/mutation via revenue court); UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (time-bound service + appeal); Registration of Births and Deaths Act 1969 (death certificate); Indian Succession Act 1925 (court succession certificate for debts/securities). Uttarakhand mirrors via UP Revenue Code as adopted + Uttarakhand RTS Act 2011.
total_days: 30-45 days (varasat mutation); 15-30 days (surviving-member certificate)

task_name: Apply for a MGNREGA Job Card (100 days of guaranteed rural wage employment)
citizen_input: Any adult member of a rural household willing to do unskilled manual work: household details and adult members' names, ages, and photographs; proof of local residence in the Gram Panchayat; and (for wage payment) Aadhaar and bank/post-office account details.
outcome: A MGNREGA Job Card (Rozgar Card) issued free of cost to the household within 15 days, bearing a unique registration number and photos of adult members. It is the entitlement document used to demand work; on written demand, employment must be provided within 15 days within 5 km of residence, failing which an unemployment allowance is payable.
legal_basis: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 (NREGA/MGNREGA): Section 3 (guarantee of 100 days' employment within 15 days of demand); Chapter II and Schedule II paras 1-9 (registration of households, verification, and issue of Job Card within 15 days, free of cost); Section 7 and Schedule II (unemployment allowance if work not provided within 15 days); Schedule II para on work within 5 km; Section 13-15 (District Programme Coordinator and Programme Officer); Section 17 (social audit by Gram Sabha); grievance/Ombudsman under MGNREGA Ombudsman Rules/Guidelines, 2009. In UP, delivery is backed by the UP Janhit Guarantee Act, 2011 (Right to Public Services / Sewa Adhikar) time-lines.
total_days: 15 days for Job Card issue (statutory); a further 15 days to be provided work after a written work-demand

task_name: Complain about bad or unserved mid-day meal (PM POSHAN) at a government school
citizen_input: School name and location; date(s) of the incident; what went wrong (not served / poor quality / short quantity / hygiene / suspected adulteration / illness); child's class; any photos.
outcome: Inspection ordered and corrective action taken (meal restored to entitled menu/quantity/quality; vendor/cook penalized or food-security allowance paid where meal was not served), with the grievance tracked to closure.
legal_basis: National Food Security Act, 2013 (Sec. 5 mid-day meal entitlement; Sec. 14-15 District Grievance Redressal Officer & State Food Commission; Sec. 16 penalty; Sec. 28-29 social audit / vigilance committees); Mid-Day Meal Rules, 2015 (school/block/district/state monitoring committees; School Management Committee); CPGRAMS for central public grievance; FSSAI / Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 for adulteration.
total_days: Approx. 30 days for CPGRAMS-routed redress; school/block action expected within days; no MDM-specific statutory limit.

task_name: Apply for a legal municipal piped-water and sewer connection (new house, UP city)
citizen_input: My new house in a UP city has no piped water or sewer line. Owner name, plot/house address and ward, registered sale deed/allotment letter, latest house-tax (property-tax) receipt or property ID, approved building/site plan, Aadhaar/ID, passport photo. If a distribution main/sewer line already runs on the street: a household tap + sewer connection request. If no main is laid yet: a network-extension / new-line request.
outcome: A sanctioned, metered legal water connection tapped from the distribution main and a sewer connection into the public sewer manhole, with billing commenced in the applicant's name — issued by the Nagar Nigam Jal Kal Vibhag (Jal Sansthan).
legal_basis: U.P. Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1975 (Act 43 of 1975) — constitutes U.P. Jal Nigam and the Jal Sansthan / Jal Kal Vibhag; governs private connections to water works and sewers and the levy of connection charges. U.P. Municipal Corporation Act, 1959 — under which the Jal Kal Vibhag operates as a department of the Nagar Nigam (merged w.e.f. 01.04.2009 in corporation cities). Service delivery and appeals: U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (designated officer + First/Second Appellate Authority). Grievance redressal: CM Helpline 1076 and IGRS Jansunwai.
total_days: ~15-45 working days where a distribution main already exists on the street (application to sanction to physical tapping); network-extension / new-line cases run several months. Indicative — the exact guaranteed day-count under the Janhit Guarantee schedule for this specific service is not verified here.

task_name: Mutation of inherited land record into heir's name (dakhil-kharij / varasat namantaran) — Uttarakhand
citizen_input: I inherited my father's land in Uttarakhand — how do I get the record of rights mutated into my name (dakhil-kharij)?
outcome: The record of rights (khatauni) is corrected to substitute the heir's name for the deceased; heir obtains an updated khatauni copy. Mutation records possession/fiscal liability, not title.
legal_basis: U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901 (as adopted by Uttarakhand) — Section 34 (obligation to report every succession/transfer of possession) and the mutation/namantaran provisions thereunder; undisputed entries attested by Naib Tehsildar, disputed successions decided by the Tehsildar (revenue court) and appealable up to the Board of Revenue. Municipal (Nagar Nikay) mutation for urban land is separately notified under the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (Urban Development Dept, 30 days).
total_days: Uncontested: commonly ~30–90 days (municipal urban mutation carries a 30-day Right-to-Service limit; no confirmed statutory day-count for rural revenue-court mutation). Contested: no fixed limit.

task_name: Get a new domestic electricity connection for a house (UP / Uttarakhand)
citizen_input: Applicant's ID proof, proof of ownership/legal occupancy of premises (registered sale deed / house-tax receipt / registry / rent agreement with owner NOC), recent photograph, connected-load requirement, and (load-dependent) a licensed electrical contractor's wiring/test report.
outcome: A sanctioned, metered domestic LT electricity connection energized at the applicant's premises, with a consumer account/number.
legal_basis: Electricity Act 2003 (ss. 43 duty to supply, 46 recovery of expenses, 47 security); UP Electricity Supply Code 2005 (UPERC) / Uttarakhand Electricity Supply Code (UERC) and each Commission's Standards of Performance regulations; UPPCL 'Jhatpat' single-window scheme (UP); UPCL online-connection scheme (Uttarakhand); state Right-to-Service laws (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar Adhiniyam 2011) where the service is notified.
total_days: ~7-15 days where no network extension is required from a complete application/paid demand note; longer (weeks) where a line/transformer extension is needed.
source: https://www.uppcl.org/; https://uppclonline.com/; https://www.uppcl.org/uppcl/en/page/jhatpat-connection; https://www.upenergy.in/upcl/en/page/new-connection; https://www.uerc.gov.in/; https://www.uperc.org/; https://cea.nic.in/electricity-act-2003/; https://jansunwai.up.nic.in/

task_name: Get a new PDS ration card issued for your household
citizen_input: Household residence proof, Aadhaar of all members, head-of-household photo, and a self-declaration that no member holds another ration card (plus surrender/deletion certificate if splitting from an existing card)
outcome: A new NFSA ration card (AAY / Priority Household or a State/non-subsidized category) issued to the household, linked to a Fair Price Shop; increasingly delivered as a downloadable e-ration card
legal_basis: National Food Security Act, 2013 (beneficiary identification and Sec. 14/15 grievance redressal); operationalized by state PDS Control Orders under the UP / Uttarakhand Food & Civil Supplies Dept; service timeline enforceable under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (and, for Uttarakhand, the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011)
total_days: 15-30 days (UP Janhit Guarantee ration-card window ~15 days; Uttarakhand field verification + issuance ~15-30 working days)

task_name: Apply for a pucca house grant under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) via the Awaas+ 2024 survey (BPL family, UP village)
citizen_input: A below-poverty-line family living in a kachcha (mud/temporary) house in a UP village wants a pucca house grant under PMAY-Gramin. Needs: Aadhaar of head + all members, Aadhaar-seeded bank account of head of family, an Android smartphone (for self-survey) or access to the Panchayat enumerator, MGNREGA job card (for convergence wage days), and four-side geo-tagged photos of the existing kachcha house.
outcome: Name added to the PMAY-G Permanent Wait List (PWL), sanction order issued, and Rs. 1.20 lakh (plain-area UP) unit assistance released in installments via DBT to the Aadhaar-linked bank account for owner-driven construction of a pucca house; plus MGNREGA wage-day convergence (90-95 days) and an SBM-G toilet grant (Rs. 12,000).
legal_basis: MoRD PMAY-G Framework for Implementation (restructured w.e.f. 1 April 2016, exclusion/eligibility criteria amended August 2024); Union Cabinet approval dated 11 August 2024 continuing PMAY-G FY 2024-25 to 2028-29 for 2 crore additional houses (PIB PRID 2044582); AwaasPlus 2024 survey (launched 17 Sept 2024, app-based self-survey from Jan 2025) for identifying households left out of SECC 2011 PWL; convergence anchored in MGNREGA (Act of 2005) and Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin. Grievance under RTI Act 2005 and CPGRAMS.
total_days: Approx. 10-14 months from survey submission to house completion in practice (survey-to-Gram-Sabha ~3-4 months; sanction-to-first-installment typically ~1 month; construction across installments ~5-6 months). Programmatic completion target ~12 months from sanction; not statutorily guaranteed.

task_name: Apply for the Post-Matric (Dashmottar) Scholarship for an SC college-going student
citizen_input: SC caste certificate, current-year admission/enrollment proof, family income certificate (below Rs 2,50,000/year for SC), previous-year marksheet, tuition-fee receipt, Aadhaar (with Aadhaar-linked mobile), and Aadhaar/NPCI-seeded bank account in the student's own name
outcome: Post-matric (Dashmottar) scholarship for the SC college student sanctioned; maintenance allowance and reimbursed compulsory fees credited by DBT to the student's Aadhaar-seeded bank account
legal_basis: Centrally Sponsored Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students (Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment guidelines), operated in Uttar Pradesh as the Dashmottar Chhatravriti Yojana by the Social Welfare Department (Samaj Kalyan Vibhag) under the state's annual SC post-matric scholarship rules/shasanadesh; disbursed by DBT through PFMS. Income ceiling for SC/ST: Rs 2,50,000/year.
total_days: Governed by the annual scheme circular, not a fixed statutory clock; verification and DBT sanction typically take several weeks to a few months after the short application window closes

task_name: Apply for the Pre-Matric SC/ST/OBC Scholarship for a school-going child
citizen_input: Child's school enrollment/bonafide certificate and class; caste (SC/ST/OBC) certificate (Tehsildar/SDM-issued); family income certificate (Tehsildar-issued, within scheme ceiling); domicile/residence proof; previous-year marksheet; Aadhaar of student and guardian; student/guardian bank account details (for DBT); passport photo; mobile and email for OTP registration.
outcome: Scholarship sanctioned and maintenance/tuition amount disbursed by Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the Aadhaar-linked bank account.
legal_basis: Centrally-sponsored Pre-Matric Scholarship schemes: for SC — Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment "Pre-Matric Scholarship to SC Students (Classes IX & X)" guidelines; for OBC/EBC — MSJE Pre-Matric Scholarship for OBC; for ST — Ministry of Tribal Affairs Pre-Matric Scholarship guidelines. State-implemented by the state Social Welfare / Backward Classes / Tribal Welfare Directorate. In Uttarakhand delivered via the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in); in Uttar Pradesh via the state portal (scholarship.up.gov.in) under state scholarship & fee-reimbursement rules. Service delivery timelines where notified fall under the state Right to Service / Sewa Adhikar / Janhit Guarantee Act schedule.
total_days: Not statutorily fixed; application windows open with the academic year (commonly Jul–Nov, renewals separate) and processing to DBT disbursement commonly spans a few months.

task_name: Register a sale deed and transfer property ownership (Uttar Pradesh)
citizen_input: How do I register a sale deed and legally transfer ownership when buying property?
outcome: Sale deed registered at the Sub-Registrar's office (conveying ownership) and, subsequently, the revenue record of rights (khatauni) and property-tax records mutated into the buyer's name via dakhil kharij (namantaran).
legal_basis: Registration Act, 1908 (esp. §17 compulsory registration of immovable-property transfers, §23 four-month presentation window, §34 enquiry/appearance of executants, §72 appeal against refusal); Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as applied in UP (stamp duty on market/circle-rate value); Uttar Pradesh Revenue Code, 2006 (§34 registering authority's intimation to Tehsildar and mutation of record of rights; §35 appeal to Sub-Divisional Officer/SDM; §210 revision to Commissioner); Income-tax Act, 1961 §194-IA (1% TDS on consideration ≥ ₹50 lakh); Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (time-bound delivery, per-service limits notified under §3, first appeal within 30 days under §6).
total_days: Registration is same-day once the Sub-Registrar appointment is reached (deed returned within days after scanning/indexing); mutation (dakhil kharij) typically 30-45 days for an undisputed case. A registered document must in any case be presented within 4 months of execution (Registration Act §23).
source: https://igrsup.gov.in/; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19960/1/english2011.pdf; https://indiankanoon.org/doc/853279/; https://indiankanoon.org/doc/186589914/; https://bor.up.nic.in/pdf/Proposed_Amendment_English.pdf; https://upbhulekh.gov.in/; https://vaad.up.nic.in/; https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/uttar-pradesh-property-registration; https://cleartax.in/s/stamp-duty-and-regi

task_name: Road-cutting permission to lay a water pipe or cable to your property
citizen_input: Property ownership proof (registry/house-tax receipt), site plan/trench sketch showing length and width of proposed cut, water-connection or utility connection details, applicant ID, and identity of the road-owning authority.
outcome: A road-cutting permit (khudai/road-cut permission) issued by the Nagar Nigam engineering wing, after payment of the road-restoration (reinstatement) deposit, allowing a trench to be dug within a stated validity window to lay the pipe or cable; the corporation restores the road and reconciles the deposit.
legal_basis: Uttar Pradesh Nagar Nigam Adhiniyam (U.P. Municipal Corporation Act), 1959 — roads/streets and laying of pipes vested in the Corporation (adopted in Uttarakhand via the U.P. Act as adapted); water supply under the U.P./Uttarakhand Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1975 (Jal Sansthan/Jal Nigam). Service-delivery timeliness and escalation under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (and the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011), enforced via the Jansunwai-Samadhan portal.
total_days: Not statutorily fixed for the road-cut permit; a few weeks in practice once the restoration deposit is paid.

task_name: Admit a child to a private school under the RTE 25% free quota (Uttar Pradesh)
citizen_input: Parent's request to admit a child to a private unaided school under the RTE 25% EWS/disadvantaged-group free quota, with: child's birth certificate, address/residence proof (ration card / voter ID / Aadhaar / electricity bill), income certificate (EWS, from e-district), caste certificate if claiming SC/ST/OBC-disadvantaged category, child's photograph, and a working mobile number for OTP.
outcome: Child admitted free of cost to the allotted private unaided school in the entry-level class (pre-primary or Class 1), with no fee, capitation, or screening; the school's cost is reimbursed by the State.
legal_basis: Section 12(1)(c) and Section 13 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (25% reservation in entry class of private unaided schools for EWS/disadvantaged groups; prohibition of screening and capitation fee), read with the Uttar Pradesh Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Rules, 2011 (as amended) and the annual RTE admission schedule notified by the UP Directorate of Basic Education / Basic Shiksha Parishad.
total_days: 45-75 days per admission round (from portal opening to school reporting); annual cycle, entry class only

task_name: File an RTI request to a state government department
citizen_input: Written application (English/Hindi/official language) describing the information sought, with the prescribed fee of Rs 10 (BPL applicants exempt on proof); no form or reason required.
outcome: The department's Public Information Officer furnishes the requested information (or a valid refusal with reasons and appeal rights), enforceable through first and second appeal.
legal_basis: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Sections 6, 5, 7, 11, 19, 20); Uttar Pradesh Right to Information Rules, 2015 (state fee/appeal rules); Uttarakhand Right to Information Rules for Uttarakhand departments.
total_days: 30 days for initial response (35 if routed via APIO; 48 hours if life/liberty; up to 40 with third-party notice); +30 days to file first appeal; +90 days to file second appeal.

task_name: Who do I complain to about an overflowing drain and uncollected garbage on my street?
citizen_input: Your street address / ward number, and the nature of the problem (overflowing drain, uncollected garbage, or both). A photo helps.
outcome: The drain is de-silted/cleared and the garbage is lifted by the corporation's sanitation and engineering wings, against a tracked complaint number, within the charter timeline.
legal_basis: Uttar Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1959 (and U.P. Municipalities Act, 1916 for smaller towns); U.P. Solid Waste (Management & Handling) and Sanitation Rules, 2019; grievance timelines per e-NagarSewa UP citizen-charter; U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (time-bound service guarantee).
total_days: Charter targets: garbage lifting ~1 day, drain/road cleaning ~24 hours; escalation adds a few days per rung.

task_name: Transfer Certificate (School Leaving Certificate) from a government school
citizen_input: Written application by parent/guardian to the school Head requesting a Transfer Certificate for the child (state name, class, admission number, receiving school / reason for move, and the destination district/state if inter-district).
outcome: A signed and sealed Transfer Certificate (School Leaving Certificate) issued by the Head of the school, drawn from the admission/scholar register, enabling admission at the receiving school. For an RTE-age (Class 1-8) child the TC must be issued immediately and free, and its absence cannot delay admission elsewhere.
legal_basis: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, Section 5 (transfer to other schools; Head Teacher shall immediately issue transfer certificate; want of TC cannot be ground to deny/delay admission; delay by Head is a disciplinary lapse). For UP: administered through the Basic Shiksha Parishad / Basic Education Department under the Uttar Pradesh Right to Service framework (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011); for Uttarakhand: Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011. Free-education duty and no-fee-for-TC follow from RTE Act ss. 3-5.
total_days: RTE-age (Class 1-8): "immediately" per RTE s.5 — commonly within a few working days in practice. Higher classes / non-RTE: no single statutory limit; ~3-7 working days is the common administrative norm.
source: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1361 (RTE Act, 2009 - full text; Section 5 on transfer and transfer certificate); https://dsel.education.gov.in/rte (Dept. of School Education & Literacy, RTE Act resources); https://edistrict.up.gov.in/ (UP e-District / Right to Service portal for notified services); https://sewasindhu.uk.gov.in/ and https://eservices.uk.gov.in/ (Uttarakhand e-service

task_name: Register a new shop under the UP Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1962
citizen_input: Establishment name and address; owner/employer ID (Aadhaar) and PAN; category of business; number of employees; date of commencement; premises address proof (rent/ownership + utility bill); photograph of premises with name board in local language; bank account proof; constitution proof (partnership deed / incorporation certificate) where applicable.
outcome: Digitally issued Registration Certificate under the UP Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1962, valid for five financial years, downloadable from Nivesh Mitra and displayed at the establishment.
legal_basis: The Uttar Pradesh Dookan Aur Vanijya Adhishthan Adhiniyam, 1962 (UP Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1962) and the U.P. Dookan Aur Vanijya Adhishthan Niyamavali, 1963; registration administered by the UP Labour Department through the Chief Inspector (appointed under Section 29), via the Nivesh Mitra single-window portal.
total_days: Apply within 30 days of commencing business; certificate typically issued within 7-15 working days (near-automatic / deemed on a valid Nivesh Mitra application).
source: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/ (The Uttar Pradesh Dookan aur Vanijya Adhishthan Adhiniyam, 1962 - India Code, official statute repository); https://prsindia.org/files/acts_states/uttar-pradesh/1962/1962UP26.pdf (UP Dookan Aur Vanijya Adhishthan Adhiniyam, 1962 - PRS India full text; defines Chief Inspector, Sec 29); https://niveshmitra.up.nic.in/ (Nivesh Mitra single-window portal,

task_name: Police verification of a new tenant (landlord-initiated tenant/PG verification)
citizen_input: Landlord's details and ownership/rent-agreement proof; tenant's name, permanent address, photo, and government photo ID (Aadhaar/passport/voter ID) plus address proof; rented property address.
outcome: A verification acknowledgement/reference number and a status of "verified / no adverse record" (clear) or an adverse report; most CCTNS portals record completion as "no adverse report" rather than issuing a formal certificate.
legal_basis: Tenant/PG verification is offered as a CCTNS citizen service by state police (UP Police lists "Tenant/PG Verification" on its citizen-services portal). The obligation to verify is imposed locally by a District Magistrate's public-order order under BNSS §163 (successor to CrPC §144), enforced by the police station under state Police Act powers. Exact mandatory-status, penalty, and SLA are set per-district by that order and are not uniform.
total_days: Locality-dependent; commonly a few days to about two weeks once the file is complete (longer for interstate tenants needing a home-district check). No uniform statutory SLA.

task_name: Transfer of ownership and re-registration of a used (purchased) vehicle
citizen_input: Used vehicle purchased from a private seller; buyer wants ownership transferred into their name and the Registration Certificate updated (and re-registered if the vehicle came from another RTO/state).
outcome: Registration Certificate (RC) re-issued showing the buyer as the registered owner; register updated at the RTO/ARTO; new registration mark assigned if inter-state.
legal_basis: Motor Vehicles Act 1988, s.50 (transfer of ownership) and s.51 (transfer where vehicle under hypothecation); Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989, rr.55-56 and Forms 28, 29, 30, 35; administered by the State Transport Department (UP / Uttarakhand) via the Regional/Assistant Regional Transport Office on the Vahan (Parivahan) portal. State Right-to-Public-Services timelines (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011) apply to service delivery windows.
total_days: 14-45 (statutory reporting window); RC re-issue typically within ~7-30 working days subject to state Right-to-Service schedule and inter-state NOC
source: https://parivahan.gov.in/parivahan/en/content/transfer-ownership; https://vahan.parivahan.gov.in/; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/9460 (Motor Vehicles Act 1988, s.50-51); https://uptransport.upsdc.gov.in/en-us/ (UP Transport Department); https://transport.uk.gov.in/ (Uttarakhand Transport Department)
